title: Exploratory feasibility study to evaluate the fundamental functionality, wear duration, and preliminary data acquisition of a novel continuous ketone monitor (CKM)
summary:
The body primarily uses sugar (glucose) as an energy source. During prolonged fasting, the metabolism changes, and the body increasingly draws on its reserves, particularly fat. The body produces so-called ketone bodies (ketones) from fat stores, which can serve as an energy source. Measuring ketones is also relevant for certain medical conditions. For this reason, new medical devices capable of continuously measuring ketones are being developed.
In this study the feasibility of continuous ketone measurement in the interstitial fluid of the subcutaneous fat tissue with a new sensor (CKM system) is examined. The investigational device is the CKM system, consisting of a sensor and sensor applicator.
For the continuous measurement of ketone bodies in the fat tissue a small sensor is inserted into the subcutaneous fat tissue on both upper arms and remains there for the duration of the study.
In addition, glucose levels are measured using another sensor, also on the upper arm. Such glucose sensors have been used for several years in the treatment of diabetes mellitus.
The CKM system is a medical device currently undergoing clinical trials and is produced by Roche Diabetes Care GmbH, Germany. It does not yet have a CE mark, which means it is not yet available on the European market. It is being used in humans for the first time.
conditions: Measurement of the metabolic parameter beta-hydroxybutyrate during fasting in healthy subjects

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Generally healthy adults aged 18 to 65 years who are able to provide written informed consent.
2. Body Mass Index (BMI) between 20 and 35 kg/m².
3. Must be willing to adhere to a study-mandated, supervised metabolic challenge to intentionally elevate ketone levels.
4. Willing and able to perform frequent capillary blood ketone/glucose testing
5. An understanding of and willingness to follow the protocol
6. Signed informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. History of type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
2. Hepatic or renal impairment: Clinically significant hepatic disease or chronic kidney disease (e.g., eGFR < 45 mL/min/1.73m²), as impaired renal and liver function directly alters beta-hydroxybutyrate clearance and metabolism.
3. Recent cardiovascular events: History of myocardial infarction, stroke, unstable angina, or severe heart failure (NYHA Class III/IV) within the past 6 months.
4. Eating disorders: History of anorexia nervosa, bulimia, or other clinically diagnosed eating disorders
5. Adrenal or thyroid dysfunction: Uncontrolled thyroid disease or adrenal insufficiency, which can disrupt normal counterregulatory hormone responses during fasting.
6. Adhesive allergies: Known severe allergy or hypersensitivity to medical-grade adhesives, silicone, or acrylics.
7. Skin abnormalities at the wear site: Presence of extensive scarring, lipohypertrophy, active eczema, psoriasis, sunburn, or tattoos at the designated sensor insertion sites (typically the abdomen or posterior upper arm), which could impair interstitial fluid diffusion.
8. Pregnancy & lactation: Currently pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the study period
9. Electromagnetic exposure: Any scheduled medical procedures during the sensor wear period that involve strong magnetic or electromagnetic fields, such as MRI, CT
scans, high-frequency electrical heat (diathermy) treatments, or X-rays.
10. Intake of cysteine; dopamine and dopamine derivative; ascorbic acid (≥500mg total daily dose); methyldopa; gentisic
acid; acetaminophen or acetyl salicylic acid (≥300mg total daily dose) within a period of three times the elimination half-life of the individual drug prior to application of the
investigational device or planned intake during the course of the clinical study
11. Anticoagulant treatment and platelet inhibition (with the exception of acetyl salicylic acid, total daily dose rate <300 mg), Phenprocoumon (e.g. Marcumar), NOAC (e.g. Dabigatran, Rivaroxaban) within 2 weeks prior to planned application of the investigational device and during the course of the clinical study
12. Any incapacity or general condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, prevents adequate compliance with the study procedures, e. g. physical, mental or visual incapacity, language barriers, alcohol or drug misuse, relevant anemia
13. Inadequate venous conditions for intravenous (IV) access on arms
14. Participation in another clinical study
15. Dependency on sponsor or investigator (e.g. co-worker or family member) or  ompanies active in the field of CGM or their subsidiaries
